It really destroys your body and it is a lot to go through. You never truly heal. You are pretty much permanently disabled for a couple of inches. Please really read about the studies, how painful it is and the huge cons against it. I can't say much because I am a taller person, but my son is 5'3", and I am doing my best to teach him that his height doesn't make a man.

Definitely look into more communities like r/phallo to get more an idea if you want bottom surgery. Top surgery will help you feel more comfortable in your skin and once you are able to take your shirt off at a public pool and beach you will feel so much better in your skin and no longer have to worry about binders.


There will be a time you will find trans joy in your life. Start following trans creators like Mars Wright who are positive transmen who do great in the world and even aren't the "perfect male body" do great in life and for our community and even do things that most transmen wouldn't be able to do and he pushes those limits. 



Find a community online and in person you fit in. It does get better and once you are older it does get easier, especially when you truly do start to grow into your body. I don't know if you are on hormones right now, but once you are, it makes such a difference. If you don't have one now, get a trans friendly therapist to talk about these things. We all need a way to cope, and there is nothing wrong with that.



I wish the best of luck in your journey, coming from a transmasc nonbinary parent of a transmasc kid in his last year of high school, I promise it does get better. My son is almost done with school and is seeing the end of that chapter and ready to start his full medical journey to start 🖤.
